title: Longest Run After Replacements
statement:
You may change **at most `k` letters** of `text` into any other lowercase letters. After the changes, look for the longest stretch of consecutive letters that are **all the same letter**.

Return the **maximum possible length** of such a stretch.
constraints: text contains only lowercase letters a-z

examples.explanation: Take the stretch aaba (positions 0 to 3) and change its one b into an a: aaaa has length 4. No stretch of length 5 can be fixed with one change.
Change both a's (or both b's): the whole text becomes one letter.

hints.nudge: A stretch can become all one letter if the number of letters that are NOT the most common one inside it is at most k.
hints.pattern: Sliding window tracking the highest letter frequency inside the window.
hints.pseudocode:
count = 26 zeros; left = 0; maxFreq = 0; best = 0
for right in 0..n-1:
  count[text[right]]++; maxFreq = max(maxFreq, count[text[right]])
  while (right - left + 1) - maxFreq > k: count[text[left]]--; left++
  best = max(best, right - left + 1)
hints.walkthrough: For a window, the cheapest way to make it uniform is to keep its most frequent letter and replace the rest, which costs (window length - highest frequency). The window is valid when that cost is at most k. Expand the right end; if the window becomes invalid, move the left end forward. You never need to lower maxFreq when shrinking: a window only matters if it beats the best length so far, which requires a larger frequency. O(n) time, O(1) space.
